title: How AI guardrails are impeding the work of offensive cybersecurity researchers
slides: Can AI guardrails block your offensive security research?
Models refuse to simulate malicious attacker commands.
Even benign payloads trigger false positive blocks.
Your tests get truncated outputs, losing critical data.
Benchmark each tool's guardrails before your next red team.
thread_text:
1. Your AI blocks your own tests.

Models now refuse to simulate malicious commands — even when you need them for security research.

2. Benign payloads, false blocks.

Simple test payloads like 'ping' trigger guardrails. You hit a wall before you even start.

3. Truncated outputs hide findings.

Your tool cuts off the response mid-command. Critical data from a red team test disappears.

4. Guardrails hurt offensive work.

Every security researcher now fights the same AI safety rules they're supposed to evaluate.

5. Benchmark each tool this week.

Take a basic red team prompt and run it on GPT, Claude, and Gemini. Which one blocks you first?
